habitat: Pairs in dense vegetation in broad-leaved woodland, dense lowveld bushveld and riverine thickets. Newman says it replaces Southern Boubou in northern areas.
summary: A fairly common resident. Black above with a white wing-bar. The whole underparts are lightly washed pinkish, with less cinnamon on the flanks and vent than other boubous. The duet is normally three liquid bell-like notes answered by hueee. Some calls cannot be told from Southern Boubou. Newman’s page uses the name Laniarius aethiopicus. The stored name Laniarius major was left unchanged. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Southern Boubou has a white throat grading to a richer cinnamon belly. Some duet calls cannot be separated.

calls.description: A duet that can sound like one bird: normally three liquid bell-like notes answered by hueee. Some calls cannot be told from Southern Boubou. Grade A call from Sigiria Forest, Nairobi, Kenya, under the name Laniarius major. The filename is XC259660-TropicalBoubou 120715.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Newman page titles the bird Tropical Boubou and uses Laniarius aethiopicus. This file keeps Laniarius major. Swamp Boubou is a comparison Newman names and is not in this list. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
